findings.title: Null dereference when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the array is empty or null. The next line then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining and throws a TypeError. This happens for any booking with a Meet location and no destination calendar, which is exactly the case the Cal Video fallback is meant to handle. handleNewBooking can also set destinationCalendar to null. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Patch of hangout link uses undefined calendarId
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` can now be undefined, because it is resolved by `find` on credentialId. The insert falls back to "primary", but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` with no fallback. When the event is created on the primary calendar and has a hangout link, the patch call fails or targets the wrong calendar, so the description never gets the Meet link. Use the same `selectedCalendar || "primary"` for the patch.

findings.title: Meaningless fallback lookup in updateEvent/deleteEvent
findings.body: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` runs its `find` only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. It then looks for a calendar whose externalId equals that falsy value, so it almost never matches. The destination-calendar fallback therefore no longer works the way it did before the array conversion (previously `destinationCalendar.externalId`). The same pattern is in deleteEvent.

findings.title: teamDestinationCalendars is read before the async map is awaited, and it mutates a shared array
findings.body: `teamDestinationCalendars` is filled inside `teamMemberPromises` callbacks. Those callbacks run synchronously inside `.map`, so the array is populated before the push, which works. However, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` mutates the array that holds `eventType.destinationCalendar`, and when the event type has no destination calendar and the organizer has none, destinationCalendar is null so the push is skipped and the team members' calendars are silently dropped. This also breaks collective events where the organizer has no calendar.

findings.title: loadUsers rewrite drops organization select and changes behavior
findings.body: The rewritten `loadUsers` removes the `organization: { select: { slug } }` selection for dynamic users, so downstream code that reads it breaks. It also throws when `dynamicUserList` is empty and wraps all errors into generic 400/500 responses. These changes are unrelated to this PR and risk regressions.

findings.title: Inverted slug condition changes org creation behavior
findings.body: The old code set `slug` when `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` and `requestedSlug` when billing was enabled. The new code sets `slug` when billing is enabled. This reverses the logic and is unrelated to the PR. Orgs will get a slug immediately under billing, bypassing the payment/verification flow, and will have no slug when billing is disabled.

findings.title: updateEvent called with undefined credential
findings.body: If the credential is not found in `this.calendarCredentials` or in the DB, or the DB credential lacks an app slug, `credential` stays undefined. It is still passed to `updateEvent(credential, ...)`, which then dereferences it (for example `credential.appName`) and throws. The outer catch then marks all references as failed. Skip the reference when no credential is found.
